governance.note: The close of the keeper-34 -> unified-engine migration: the nyiso-38 probe config (keeper-34-exact offer curve, gas_hub_basis_daily + gas_hub_basis_overlay, NYISO zonal gas basis, local-selfsupply, energy+reserve co-opt, unified continuous-temperature-ramp reliability floor) plus --priced-interchange, the keeper-34 flag the migration template had silently dropped. ROOT CAUSE OF THE nyiso-36/37/38 C1 FAILS: keeper 34's run_config.json records priced_interchange=true (explicitly passed; NYISO resolves to False by default in both code eras). Without it, BOTH --nyiso-firm-imports and --nyiso-import-reconciliation are hard-gated off (run_calibration.py 'if priced_interchange and ...'), so the probes silently ran a different market: measured EIA-930 interchange netted into demand as a fixed hourly subtraction, no priced import node, no HQ firm must-flow floor, no monthly reconciliation band. The fixed import schedule displaced exactly the un-floored mid-merit supply (downstate gas steam). Restoring the flag recovers 2024 ST_GAS 8.89 -> 9.41 TWh and clears both 2023 C1 fails (CC_REGULAR +2.61 -> +1.06, ST_GAS -1.30 -> -0.86). MIGRATION FIDELITY (all verified against keeper sha 180d579, recovered by deepening the shallow clone): resolve_priced_interchange identical; interchange unification (f04bad2d) byte-identical for NYISO (import tranches, per-year ladders, export sink, firm floors HQ 1.0 / IESO 0.0, node links 3000/1000/1200 MW, EFORd 0.0, recon band 0.02; inject_nyiso_firm_imports and build_import_node_reconciliation behaviorally unchanged); reserve co-opt unification (6323221a) byte-identical for NYISO (RCPF ladder, 7 locational families, eligibility masks incl. ST_GAS 30-min-only, spin fraction 0.5, 57 ORDC steps $62-$775, P+R<=pmax untouched); topology + Central-East TTC tables identical; nyiso_zonal_gas_hub.csv (SOM Figure A-6) unchanged; keeper-34's dirty diff (when-available floor coefficients + Ravenswood outage routing) already migrated. ONE POST-KEEPER STRUCTURAL ADDITION KEPT PER RULE #10: the measured NYISO simultaneous-import limit (NYISO_simultaneous_import, 4,350 MW, Gold Book / IRM-LCR) now caps aggregate flow across the 5.2 GW of border links; under the monthly EIA-930 reconciliation band it shifts some import volume from peak to off-peak hours, which accounts for the modest ST_GAS delta vs keeper 34 (2024: 9.41 vs 9.80; both inside the C1 band) and part of the deeper 2023 mean-LMP caveat. PREMISE CORRECTION recorded for the ledger: the prior handoff's claim that keeper 34 dispatched ~1.2 TWh of Capital_Hudson steam is wrong - keeper 34's committed payload shows 0.157 TWh model CH ST in 2024 (Bowline 0.10 / Roseton 0.06); the ~1.2-1.6 TWh figure is the measured CAMPD ACTUAL, which keeper 34 under-ran identically (r=0.30). The Bowline/Roseton under-run inside a passing class total is a pre-existing shared open item (Iroquois Z2 annual-mean basis vs summer spread compression is the leading candidate), not a migration regression; any future fix must be a measured input (SOM monthly basis), never a floor or offer adder. C1 note: the authoritative rubric volume band is +/-min(1% ISO load, 5 TWh) = +/-1.50 TWh for NYISO; the +/-1.35 band quoted by prior probe sessions was the quick-probe's 1%-of-generation approximation.

_migration_status: The unified-engine migration is COMPLETE and NYISO again holds a reproducible determination on current main: C1 (HARD) passes every scorable year - 2024 ST_GAS -1.40 TWh (band +/-1.50), 2023 ST_GAS -0.86, 2023 CC_REGULAR +1.06, 2024 CC_REGULAR -0.44 - with C2, C4 (gas r=0.99/0.99, 2025 in tolerance) and C5a CO2 in band all years. 2025 gas classes are SKIPPED (preliminary EIA-923 vintage, 15-70% plant reporting), governed by C2 which passes. The open items are the SAME three SOFT price criteria keeper 34 ledgered - the reserve-scarcity (ORDC) + min-gen-floor frontier: C3a mean LMP -15.6/-19.2/-13.2%, C3b duration NRMSE 0.211/0.304/0.203, C3c >$300 tail 0h vs 10/12/42h. 2023 C3a is deeper than keeper 34 (-15.6 vs -8.0): the priced node's elastic imports soften off-peak 2023 prices ~6pp vs the measured-schedule probe (-9.5%), amplified by the SIL cap shifting reconciled import volume off-peak. Same documented frontier (confirmed non-closable with grounded inputs by nyiso-29/31); kept per rule #1, not chased per rule #12 (ST_GAS lands UNDER actual every scored year, so the floor is not over-forced). NET DETERMINATION: CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS - calibrated on the hard axes (per-class volume, system volume, dispatch correlation, CO2) with the price criteria as ledgered reserve-scarcity-frontier caveats, at keeper-34 caveat count (3 soft).
